articles.title: Percentage: formulas and methods
articles.content:
## Core formulas
- x% of y = xy/100
- Percentage change = (new − old)/old × 100
- New value after an increase of p% = old × (1+p/100)
- New value after a decrease of p% = old × (1−p/100)

**Method:** identify the base quantity before calculating a percentage. Successive percentage changes apply to the updated value, not always the original value.

questions.q: What is 5% of ₹237?
A salary of ₹274 increases by 8%. What is the new salary?
A machine priced at ₹311 is discounted by 12%. Find its price after discount.
A quantity changes from 348 to 295.8. What is the percentage change?
questions.explanation: Percentage change = (295.8 − 348)/348 × 100 = -15%, hence a 15% decrease.

articles.title: Problems on Trains: formulas and methods
articles.content:
## Core formulas
- Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18.
- Time to pass a pole = train length / speed.
- Time to cross a platform = (train length + platform length) / speed.
- Opposite-direction relative speed = sum of speeds; same-direction relative speed = difference of speeds.

**Method:** express all lengths in metres and speeds in metres per second before calculating time.

questions.q: A train 113 m long travels at 36 km/h. How long does it take to pass a signal post?
questions.explanation: Speed = 36 × 5/18 = 10.00 m/s. Time = length/speed = 113/10.00 ≈ 11.30 seconds.

questions.q: A 130 m train moving at 39 km/h crosses a 78 m platform. Find the time taken.
questions.explanation: Distance covered = 130+78 = 208 m. Speed = 10.83 m/s. Time = 208/10.83 ≈ 19.20 seconds.

questions.q: Two trains of lengths 147 m and 117 m approach each other at 42 km/h and 28 km/h. Approximately how long do they take to cross?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = (42+28)×5/18 = 19.44 m/s. Total length = 264 m; time ≈ 13.58 seconds.

questions.explanation: Speed = 45 × 5/18 = 12.50 m/s. Time = length/speed = 164/12.50 ≈ 13.12 seconds.

## Approach
- Identify the word's meaning in context before looking at the options.
- Eliminate choices that are related but not equivalent.
- Consider tone and intensity: two words may be similar without being interchangeable in every sentence.

**Practice tip:** learn words in context, including common collocations and connotations.

articles.title: Number Series: identifying patterns
articles.content:
## Common patterns
- Constant addition or subtraction
- Multiplication or division
- Increasing differences
- Squares, cubes, and other sequences
- Each term formed from earlier terms

**Method:** calculate consecutive differences first; if they are not constant, inspect ratios and second differences.

articles.title: Syllogisms: valid conclusions
articles.content:
## Approach
- Treat the statements as true, even if they conflict with real-world knowledge.
- Use only information guaranteed by the statements.
- Distinguish 'all', 'some', and 'none'; do not reverse an inclusion unless it is stated.

**Method:** use set diagrams or carefully track which groups are included, overlapping, or disjoint.

questions.q: Statements: All architects are designers. All designers are creative. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 1]
questions.explanation: The inclusion chain architects ⊆ designers ⊆ creative means all architects are creative.

questions.q: Statements: No pilots are careless. Some trainees are pilots. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 2]
questions.explanation: The trainees who are pilots cannot be careless.

questions.q: Statements: All orchids are plants. No plants are machines. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 3]
questions.explanation: Orchids are plants, and plants are excluded from machines.

questions.q: Statements: Some editors are musicians. All musicians are patient. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 4]
options: Some patient people are not musicians.
questions.explanation: The editors who are musicians must be patient.

questions.q: Statements: All tablets are devices. Some devices are portable. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 5]
questions.explanation: The first conclusion is exactly a premise; the statement about some portable devices does not imply all tablets are portable.

questions.q: Statements: No reptiles are warm-blooded. All geckos are reptiles. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 6]
questions.explanation: Geckos are reptiles, and reptiles are not warm-blooded.

questions.q: Statements: Some nurses are researchers. No researchers are careless. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 7]
questions.explanation: Nurses who are researchers cannot be careless.

questions.q: Statements: All copper objects are conductive. This wire is a copper object. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 8]
questions.explanation: The wire is copper, and all copper objects are conductive.

questions.q: Statements: All copper objects are conductive. This wire is a copper object. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 24]
questions.explanation: The wire is copper, and all copper objects are conductive.

questions.q: Statements: All architects are designers. All designers are creative. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 25]
questions.explanation: The inclusion chain architects ⊆ designers ⊆ creative means all architects are creative.

questions.q: Statements: No pilots are careless. Some trainees are pilots. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 26]
questions.explanation: The trainees who are pilots cannot be careless.

questions.q: Statements: All orchids are plants. No plants are machines. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 27]
questions.explanation: Orchids are plants, and plants are excluded from machines.

questions.q: Statements: Some editors are musicians. All musicians are patient. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 28]
options: Some patient people are not musicians.
questions.explanation: The editors who are musicians must be patient.

questions.q: Statements: All tablets are devices. Some devices are portable. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 29]
questions.explanation: The first conclusion is exactly a premise; the statement about some portable devices does not imply all tablets are portable.

questions.q: Statements: No reptiles are warm-blooded. All geckos are reptiles. Which conclusion necessarily follows? [Set 30]
questions.explanation: Geckos are reptiles, and reptiles are not warm-blooded.
